symptoms: Young seedlings may topple over and die because the stem is damaged near the soil.
Leaves show irregular brown or grayish spots and may turn yellow and fall off.
Stems develop dark brown sunken spots that can cause the plant to fall over.
Fruits show small pale sunken spots that grow to cover the whole fruit.
Infected fruits eventually turn into a soft watery mass or become black and mummified.
favourable_conditions: The disease thrives in temperatures around 29 degrees Celsius.
prevention: Always get your seeds from healthy fruits.
Treat seeds with hot water at 50 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes before planting.
Rotate brinjal with other crops like paddy or gingelly instead of planting it in the same spot every year.
Plough your fields deeply during the summer to reduce the disease in the soil.
practices: Remove and destroy all parts of the plant that show signs of the disease.
Clear away all old plant debris from the field to stop the spread.
Monitor your plants regularly for any signs of spots or rot.
